In the triangle above, the value of $y$ is{{field-1}}${}^{∘}.$
question.worked_solution:
First, from the diagram, notice that $∠BCA$ and $∠BCD$ are supplementary. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠BCA+m∠BCD & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠BCA+y & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠BCA & ={180}^{∘}-y.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $△ABC$ is an isosceles triangle where $\overset{―}{AC}≅\overset{―}{BC}$, the base angles must be equal:

$$
m∠B=m∠A={56}^{∘}.
$$

Finally, since the interior angles of any triangle sum to ${180}^{∘},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠A+m∠B+m∠BCA & ={180}^{∘} \\ {56}^{∘}+{56}^{∘}+({180}^{∘}-y) & ={180}^{∘} \\ y & ={112}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$
